text:
The Kraken sent Shane Wright to Nashville for Matthew Wood, closing the book on the fourth overall pick of 2022 and opening one on a Lethbridge-born winger. It's the kind of move that tells you who management believes in, and right now that's Berkly Catton, 20, who has 10 points in his last ten games and a seven-game point streak through the Calgary win.

The record, 9-6-1, flatters the team. Seattle takes 45 percent of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and its shooters have scored about 10 more goals than those chances predict. Our race model says the Kraken have banked 4.3 points their play didn't earn, and our simulations still give them only 35 percent for the playoffs.

The bigger worry is that the shooting luck has been covering bad goaltending. Philipp Grubauer has saved 4.8 goals fewer than expected over his last five starts, Joey Daccord 3.7 fewer. When the finishing cools, and it will, somebody has to stop pucks. Jared McCann's injury, "a blow for sure" in Pacific North Hockey's headline, takes a scorer out of a lineup that needs every one. Matty Beniers' overtime winner against Calgary was a nice night. The Jordan Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann line, at 39 percent of the chances, is the problem to solve.
headline: Seattle traded a former fourth pick and found a new kid
